summary_paragraph: A woman with type 2 diabetes and a recent hospitalization for nausea and acute kidney injury was readmitted with fever, severe crampy abdominal pain, and watery diarrhea. The infectious workup was negative, and symptoms resolved quickly, but persistent nausea and inability to tolerate food raised concern for gastroparesis. A gastric emptying study confirmed delayed gastric emptying. She was managed with high-dose ondansetron, dietary modifications, and discontinuation of labetalol due to bradycardia. She advanced to a full diet, had constipation resolved with laxatives, and was discharged home in improved condition with a lactose-free diet and follow-up plan.
